comments.body: Looks like several other `*_like()` ops have the same issue (e.g. `rand_like()`, `randint_like()`, `randn_like()`, `zeros_like()`, `ones_like()`, etc.). `empty_like()` seems to give the correct strides though.

Inductor decomposition for `full_like` does not preserve the strides. It's probably best to use `torch.full(x.shape).as_strided(x.shape, x.stride())` in the decomposition instead of `torch.full(x.shape).to(memory_format)` since `memory_format` is insufficient to express all types of strides.

Note that the documentation https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.full_like.html supports the output of inductor and eager goes against the documentation. I guess the documentation is wrong and eager implementation should be the reference.

@bdhirsh between this and the other stride mismatch problem in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/144736 I would like to figure out why our debug executor isn't working for this case. cc @shunting314
I started a PR in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/144765, but it has test failures.

@ezyang - I can add that back as an option. the problem is, we have many incorrect strides for aten. these are often false positives in determining the error. an incorrect stride for a custom op will always be an error but an incorrect stride for a aten op may not matter.

See, this other issue I added: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/139312 I was debugging a model, hit this which didn't matter, and then turned off asserts for aten ops because it was a false positive. And another recent one - https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/144187, which was passing, then now is incorrect allow export.


Similarly, look at all these meta failures after I 
enable py dispatcher in fake tensor: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/138953.

@eellison could you argue why "incorrect stride for aten op may not matter"? It seems to me like all of these are handguns waiting to fire (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/144736 is a good example where the existence of an Inductor lowering meant that *most* of the time the stride didn't matter, except when only sometimes you did do a fallback and then the correct stride did matter.) Is your claim something like, we don't need accurate strides as long as Inductor is actually going to lower everything else? Can we operationalize this in a way so that the asserts don't have false positives.

The alternative, which I really don't mind at all, is to get our strides exactly correct everywhere.

> "incorrect stride for aten op may not matter"

It will only matter if :

- We lower the op (through decomp or lowering) but the output stride is wrong for some later operator which needs the correct stride
- We don't lower the op - then it will always be incorrect.

If you set `torch._functorch.config.fake_tensor_crossref == "all"` and use bisector or use `backend=aot_eager_decomp_partition_crossref` than we'll check all ops. otherwise it will ignore aten/prims. 

I would be happy if we fixed all the strides, but we're not there yet.

> If you set torch._functorch.config.fake_tensor_crossref == "all" and use bisector or use backend=aot_eager_decomp_partition_crossref than we'll check all ops. otherwise it will ignore aten/prims.

> I would be happy if we fixed all the strides, but we're not there yet.

Do you think running these with OpInfos and burning down failures would get us most of the way there? (We have a BE week coming up)

We already do run them with [opinfos](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e2251fffbb012303f1c47ead67fa733a49fd21b4/test/test_ops.py#L2801-L2812). But we can file some more issues for the additional errors that are exposed when enabling PyDispatcher.
"There is a general problem that metas have incorrect strides. This particular one bit us twice, so we should UBN this, but general problem for meta strides"

@isuruf I see some semi-recent comments here from you. Were you planning to keep going with this? (Got bumped up in priority during internal triage, so if you're not actively working I'll try to take it over)
Go ahead. I'm not actively working on it.

> any update ?

@eellison I've been trying to explore if we can solve it with a permute, as you suggested offline. I think you mentioned that it depends on whether full_like reproduces strides exactly or if it just preserves stride permutation? I _think_ it's the latter. For example, I have this:
```
>>> import torch
>>> x = torch.rand(4, 3)[::2, :]
>>> x = x.permute(1, 0)
>>> x.shape, x.stride()
(torch.Size([3, 2]), (1, 6))
>>>
>>> y = torch.full_like(x, 1)
>>> y.shape, y.stride()
(torch.Size([3, 2]), (1, 3))
```

So I think it's safe to implement a permute-based solution? If so, then I'm wrestling with test failures right now. But is there anything else you'd suggest to validate beyond my slicing example here?

> I think you mentioned that it depends on whether full_like reproduces strides exactly or if it just preserves stride permutation? 

It's the latter. When you do a `full_like` with a diagonal view as input, the result is a contiguous tensor.
Last time I looked at it, `full_like` behaves exactly like `empty_like` and `empty_like` uses `empty_permuted`.

```
import torch

def f(x):
    return torch.full_like(x, 3)

x = torch.randn(4, 5, 6).transpose(1, -1)
out = f(x)
out_compiled = torch.compile(f, backend="aot_eager_decomp_partition")(x)
print(out.stride())
print(out_compiled.stride())
# prints
# (30, 1, 6)
# (30, 5, 1)
```

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Incorrect Strides can manifest in errors within torch.compile. Potentially what makes them trickier is that they only sometimes cause errors. An incorrect stride can lay dormant for a while and then cause a problem. 

See, [this discussion](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/144699#issuecomment-2591018702) with @ezyang, @bdhirsh and myself about incorrect strides.


There are a number of known issues that yet unfixed. Some of them have outstanding prs, please check with the pr author before taking it on.

- [x] `full_like`: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/144699
- [ ] `_unsafe_index` : https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/139312
- [x] `_fft_r2c`: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/135087
- [ ] `_constant_pad_nd`: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/144187

Additionally, there are a number of stride & other issues that have been exposed by enabling PyDispatcher in FakeTensorMode. This causes us to potentially route through different decompositions and metas. It is what we use in torch.compile, which means we lack coverage of this mode in our other tests.
 
Tests exposed by this [turning this on](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/138953#issuecomment-2438965279):
- [ ] dropout
- [ ] MultiLabelMarginLoss


Fft tests as well, but that might be related to `_fft_r2c` in the existing issue.

issue.title: incorrect _unsafe_index meta

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When I'm working on this [PR](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/140399), I meet a test failed case `python test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py TestInductorOpInfoCUDA.test_comprehensive_fft_hfftn_cuda_float16`, it's related to `constant_pad_nd` op.


## Summary
I found there is two potential dispatched methods for `constant_pad_nd` when run it directly with `meta` device and run it in `inductor` and they didn't return the same tensor.

## Code
1. Directly run it with `meta` device:
```
import torch

a = torch.empty_strided((2, 4, 5), (20, 1, 4), dtype=torch.complex128, device='meta')
print(a.shape)
print(a.stride())
b = torch.constant_pad_nd(a, [0, 0, 0, -2, 0, 0])
print(b.shape)
print(b.stride())
```
If we run the above code, we could see for any of `meta`, `cuda` and `cpu` device, it will print:
```
torch.Size([2, 4, 5])
(20, 1, 4)
torch.Size([2, 2, 5])
(10, 1, 2)
```
So the `meta` device matches the `cpu` and `cuda` device, it do **meet our expectation**.

2. torch.compile:
We run `constant_pad_nd` with same arguments but run it with compiled.
```
import torch

a = torch.empty_strided((2, 4, 5), (20, 1, 4), dtype=torch.complex128, device='cuda')

def foo(a):
    b = torch.constant_pad_nd(a, [0, 0, 0, -2, 0, 0])
    return b

new_foo = torch.compile(foo)
new_foo(a)
```
We could try to print the graph of ir:
![forward_decomp](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31b4f87d-4746-4571-a012-7106d9fd6edf)

We could see in the pink box, the stride of `constant_pad_nd` is **`(10, 5, 1)`**, it's **not aligned** with the stride above **`(10, 1, 2)`**, so we could image there is mismatch in the meta function for directly run and run it in `inductor`.

## Analysis
### call stack
I tried to debug the two different behavior, I found both of the two approaches will go to:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/816328fa51382e9b50e60fb928a690d5c1bdadaf/torch/_prims_common/wrappers.py#L290-L291
but they may have different `fn`
1. Directly run it with `meta` device:
it will go to some function called `empty_like`:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/816328fa51382e9b50e60fb928a690d5c1bdadaf/torch/_refs/__init__.py#L4972-L5010
In this method, it will keep the output's stride aligned with the `cpu` or `cuda` device.
2. torch.compile:
It will go to some function called `constant_pad_nd`:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/816328fa51382e9b50e60fb928a690d5c1bdadaf/torch/_refs/__init__.py#L2901-L2981
In this method, it seems it didn't keep the stride align with the `cpu` or `cuda` device.

### my guess
I suspected it was caused when we initialize meta function for each op, because it seems we didn't have a meta function for `constant_pad_nd`, so pytorch skip some setup here:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/816328fa51382e9b50e60fb928a690d5c1bdadaf/torch/_meta_registrations.py#L6921-L6926

## Potential solution
I'm not very clear if it's an expected behavior, if it's not, there are two potential solution in my mind:
1. Ask `inductor` to call the `empty_like` in the above.
2. Introduce a meta function `meta_constant_pad_nd` for this op and make it run in both of the two places mentioned above.

WDYT? Any help would be very appreciated! Thank you!
